definitions.explanation: The upward force exerted by a fluid on an object immersed in it. A fundamental concept in physics, also used more broadly to describe the ability of something to float.

examples.japanese: {浮力|ふりょく}で{体|からだ}が{浮|う}く。
examples.english: The body floats due to buoyancy.

examples.japanese: {塩水|しおみず}は{真水|まみず}より{浮力|ふりょく}が{大|おお}きい。
examples.english: Salt water has greater buoyancy than fresh water.

examples.japanese: {船|ふね}が{沈|しず}まないのは、{水|みず}の{浮力|ふりょく}が{船|ふね}の{重|おも}さを{支|ささ}えているからだ。
examples.english: Ships don't sink because the buoyancy of the water supports the weight of the ship.

notes:
A physics term that learners encounter in science contexts. The concept is explained by Archimedes' principle: an object submerged in fluid experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the displaced fluid.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {浮力|ふりょく}が{働|はたら}く: buoyancy acts/works
- {浮力|ふりょく}が{大|おお}きい: has high buoyancy
- {浮力|ふりょく}を{利用|りよう}する: to make use of buoyancy
- {水|みず}の{浮力|ふりょく}: buoyancy of water

RELATED WORDS:
- {重力|じゅうりょく}: gravity — the downward force that buoyancy counteracts
- {水圧|すいあつ}: water pressure — pressure exerted by water
- {比重|ひじゅう}: specific gravity — the ratio of a substance's density to that of water
